answer: A reputation system can be subverted by a flood of fabricated identities, so the lowest point of trust must be defined before scoring begins. That nadir is where an account has zero witnessed work and no countersignatures from established peers. Every new key starts there. To anchor trust, the protocol ties influence to tenure: only accounts with verified contributions across many epochs gain standing to vote. Because influence grows by witnessed labor rather than sheer key count, a canyon of synthetic accounts stays stuck at the nadir together.
